title: Practice: ADF, Fabric, Databricks and Unity Catalog
summary: 8 questions on ADF objects and variables, idempotent reruns, managed identity, OneLake, Delta, medallion layers and Unity Catalog. Practice and review, without a timer.
provenance: Prepared by Claude Code on 2026-09-24 from the AtlasNote V3 seed; original questions, no private data or third-party text. Owner review required before publication.

qcm.title: Practice: ADF, Fabric, Databricks and Unity Catalog

questions.prompt: In Azure Data Factory, which object holds the connection information (endpoint, authentication, integration runtime) that datasets and activities use?

options.text: Linked service
Dataset
options.explanation: A dataset describes data structure/location and points to a linked service.

options.text: Trigger
options.explanation: A trigger decides when a pipeline starts.

options.text: Pipeline parameter
options.explanation: Parameters pass run inputs; they can feed a linked service but do not define it.

questions.explanation: Linked services describe connections, datasets describe data, activities do work, pipelines compose activities and triggers start them.

links.label: Review: Azure Data Factory pipeline mental model

questions.prompt: Inside an ADF ForEach that runs its iterations in parallel, every iteration uses Set Variable on the same pipeline variable. What is the risk?

options.text: Iterations overwrite each other's value, because the variable belongs to the pipeline run rather than to one iteration.
None; each iteration gets an isolated copy of the variable.
options.explanation: Pipeline variables are shared by all iterations of the run.

options.text: The pipeline is rejected when it is published.
options.explanation: It deploys; the problem appears at runtime as nondeterministic values.

options.text: The pipeline parameters are modified.
options.explanation: Parameters are fixed for the run; variables are the mutable state.

questions.explanation: Keep per-item state inside the iteration (for example activity outputs or item() values), or run the loop sequentially when a shared variable is unavoidable.

links.label: Review: ADF parameters, variables and expressions

questions.prompt: A daily load may be retried after a transient failure. Which designs make a rerun safe? Select all that apply.

options.text: Write to a run-scoped staging location, validate it, then promote it atomically.
Overwrite the date partition being loaded, or MERGE on a business key.
Append the whole source file to the target table again.
options.explanation: Appending again duplicates the rows that were already written.

options.text: Retry indefinitely when a data-quality rule fails.
options.explanation: Deterministic failures do not fix themselves; alert instead.

questions.explanation: Idempotent writes let the same input produce the same target state no matter how often the run is repeated.

questions.prompt: A pipeline in Azure Data Factory must read files from ADLS Gen2. Which authentication approach is preferred?

options.text: The factory's managed identity with a role assignment or ACL scoped to the required container or folder.
The storage account key pasted into the linked service.
options.explanation: A long-lived, all-powerful shared secret in configuration.

options.text: The account key stored in Key Vault.
options.explanation: Better than inline, but it is still a shared key; use it only when identity-based access is impossible.

options.text: A SAS token without expiry passed as a pipeline parameter.
options.explanation: Non-expiring tokens in parameters leak easily into logs and run history.

questions.explanation: Managed identities remove stored secrets; grant them least privilege. Key Vault is for secrets that cannot be avoided.

links.label: Review: managed identity and Key Vault

questions.prompt: What does a OneLake shortcut do in Microsoft Fabric?

options.text: It references data in another location so Fabric items can use it without copying it.
It copies the target data into OneLake every night.
options.explanation: Shortcuts are references, not scheduled copies.

options.text: It creates a backup of a lakehouse.
It removes the need to manage permissions on the underlying source.
options.explanation: Access to the target still has to be designed and granted.

questions.explanation: Shortcuts unify access across storage locations; security of the workspace, the item and the underlying data must be designed together.

links.label: Review: Fabric OneLake and lakehouse mental model

questions.prompt: Which statements about Delta tables are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: The transaction log records each committed version; readers see a consistent snapshot of one version.
VACUUM deletes data files that are no longer referenced and older than the retention threshold, which can make older versions unavailable for time travel.
Delta stores table data as CSV files.
options.explanation: Data files are Parquet; the log adds transactional metadata.

options.text: Appending a DataFrame whose column has an incompatible type silently changes the table schema.
options.explanation: Schema enforcement rejects the write; schema changes have to be requested explicitly.

questions.explanation: The _delta_log makes writes atomic and versioned. Retention and VACUUM settings decide how far back time travel works.

questions.prompt: In a medallion design, where do deduplication and conformance to validated types primarily belong?

options.text: Bronze
options.explanation: Bronze keeps source fidelity and ingestion metadata so you can replay.

options.text: Silver
Gold
options.explanation: Gold serves business aggregates built on already-validated Silver data.

options.text: Only in the BI tool
options.explanation: Pushing cleaning downstream repeats it in every report.

questions.explanation: Silver is the validated, conformed and deduplicated layer; Gold builds business-ready products on top of it.

links.label: Review: Bronze, Silver and Gold contracts

questions.prompt: How is a table addressed in Unity Catalog SQL, and who should normally receive privileges on it?

options.text: catalog.schema.table, with privileges granted to groups or service principals.
schema.table, with privileges granted to each individual user.
options.explanation: The namespace has three levels, and per-user grants are hard to review.

options.text: workspace.catalog.table, with privileges granted to groups.
options.explanation: The workspace is not part of the name.

options.text: metastore.schema.table, with privileges granted to the table owner only.

questions.explanation: Unity Catalog uses a three-level namespace under a metastore. Granting to groups and service principals keeps access reviewable.
